lines.text: | MS-01 | **The state just before the anger.** Haman went out "joyful and glad of heart. But when Haman saw Mordecai … he was filled with wrath" (Est 5:9). Uzziah "grew proud, to his destruction" (2Ch 26:16; *lēḇ* in the text) before his anger at the priests (26:19). "the haughtiness of his heart" before Moab's insolence (Jer 48:29). | Est 5:9; 2Ch 26:16; Jer 48:29 | U1 §38 point 5; part M | Ch 4 |

| MS-02 | **Where anger is kept, devised and planned.** "The godless in heart cherish anger" (Job 36:13). "with perverted heart devises evil, continually sowing discord" (Pro 6:14). "Esau said to himself" (*lēḇ*), "then I will kill my brother Jacob" (Gen 27:41). | Job 36:13; Pro 6:14; Gen 27:41 | U1 §38; part M | Ch 4 |
| MS-03 | **Where anger is taken in counsel.** "I took counsel with myself" (Neh 5:7; *lēḇ* in the text), and then "I brought charges against the nobles". | Neh 5:7 | part M | Ch 4 |
| MS-04 | **Aimed at God.** "When a man's folly brings his way to ruin, his heart rages against the Lord" (Pro 19:3). | Pro 19:3 | U1 §38 | Ch 4 (10.13 has it) |

| MS-05 | **Vexation borne in the heart.** "even in the night his heart does not rest" (Ecc 2:23). "by sadness of face the heart is made glad" (Ecc 7:3). "Remove vexation from your heart" (Ecc 11:10). | Ecc 2:23; 7:3; 11:10 | U1 §38 | Ch 4 |

| MS-06 | **Before another's anger.** "do not let your heart be faint … at the fierce anger of Rezin" (Isa 7:4), after "the heart of Ahaz and the heart of his people shook" (7:2). | Isa 7:4; 7:2 | U1 §38; D3a | Ch 4 |
| MS-07 | **The angry one reads another's heart wrongly.** Eliab to David: "I know your presumption and the evil of your heart" (1Sa 17:28). | 1Sa 17:28 | U1 §38 (a misreading) | Ch 4 |

| MS-08 | **The provoking heart.** Solomon, "because his heart had turned away from the Lord" (1Ki 11:9). "Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah" (Psa 95:8). "They always go astray in their heart" (Heb 3:10). "he went on backsliding in the way of his own heart" (Isa 57:17). "They made their hearts diamond-hard" (Zec 7:12). "because of your hard and impenitent heart you are storing up wrath" (Rom 2:5). | 1Ki 11:9; Psa 95:8; Heb 3:10; Isa 57:17; Zec 7:12; Rom 2:5 | U2 §66; U1 §38 | Ch 4 |

| MS-09 | **The heart that turns it.** "Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the Lord … in order that his fierce anger may turn away from us" (2Ch 29:10). "But Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart" (2Ch 32:26). "because your heart was penitent" (2Ki 22:19). "rend your hearts and not your garments" (Joe 2:13). "Circumcise yourselves to the Lord; remove the foreskin of your hearts" (Jer 4:4). | 2Ch 29:10; 32:26; 2Ki 22:19; Joe 2:13; Jer 4:4 | U2 §66, §65 point 3 | Ch 4 |
| MS-10 | **The heart that does not take it in.** "it burned him up, but he did not take it to heart" (Isa 42:25). | Isa 42:25 | U2 §66 | Ch 4 (already: one mention) |

| MS-11 | **The heart that rejoices** when God acts for it: "You shall see, and your heart shall rejoice" (Isa 66:14). Aaron, sent beside Moses under God's anger: "when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart" (Exo 4:14). | Isa 66:14; Exo 4:14 | U2 §66 | Ch 4 |
| MS-12 | **Another's hardened heart as the object.** Jesus "looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart" (Mar 3:5). | Mar 3:5 | U1 §38 | Ch 4 (10.13 has it) |

| MS-13 | **The heart cut by a word.** At Stephen's speech, "they were enraged" (Act 7:54); the Greek has *sawn through in their hearts* (U1 §37). | Act 7:54 | U1 §38 (hidden by the translation) | Ch 4 |
| MS-14 | **God troubles the nations' hearts:** "I will trouble the hearts of many peoples" (Eze 32:9). | Eze 32:9 | U1 §38 | Ch 4 |
| MS-15 | **God's heart** with his anger (Hos 11:8; Jer 23:20; Isa 63:4). | as 10.13 | 10.13 | Ch 4, pointer to 10.13 |

| MS-16 | **Ruled, or quick.** "he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city" (Pro 16:32). "he who has a hasty temper exalts folly" (Pro 14:29; *ruach*). "Be not quick in your spirit to become angry" (Ecc 7:9). "the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit" (Ecc 7:8). "he who has a cool spirit is a man of understanding" (Pro 17:27). | Pro 16:32; 14:29; Ecc 7:9; 7:8; Pro 17:27 | U1 §38; D3a | Ch 6 (already: 16:32, 14:29) |

| MS-17 | **Heated, provoked.** "I went in bitterness in the heat of my spirit" (Eze 3:14). "his spirit was provoked within him as he saw that the city was full of idols" (Act 17:16). | Eze 3:14; Act 17:16 | U1 §38 | Ch 6 |
| MS-18 | **Pressed until it speaks.** Elihu, angry: "the spirit within me constrains me" (Job 32:18), and "I must speak, that I may find relief" (32:20). | Job 32:18, 20 | U1 §6 (D3a) | Ch 6 |

| MS-19 | **Embittered, and the lips rash.** "for they made his spirit bitter, and he spoke rashly with his lips" (Psa 106:33). Whose spirit is not determinable (Moses' or God's; U2 §2). | Psa 106:33 | U2 §2 | Ch 6, stated as open |
| MS-20 | **Receiving God's anger.** "the arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison" (Job 6:4). | Job 6:4 | U2 §66 | Ch 6 |

| MS-21 | **What would faint, and so restrains the anger.** "nor will I always be angry; for the spirit would grow faint before me, and the breath of life that I made" (Isa 57:16). Moses' plea: "O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?" (Num 16:22). | Isa 57:16; Num 16:22 | U2 §66 | Ch 6 |

| MS-22 | **God's Spirit comes, and anger follows.** "And the Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled" (1Sa 11:6). Samson (Judg 14:19). | 1Sa 11:6; Judg 14:19 | U1 §38 (divine, received) | Ch 6 (10.13 has it) |

| MS-23 | **Refuses the company of the angry.** "Let my soul come not into their council; O my glory, be not joined to their company. For in their anger they killed men" (Gen 49:6). | Gen 49:6 | U1 §38 point 6 | Ch 5 |
| MS-24 | **Snared by learning an angry man's ways:** "lest you learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare" (Pro 22:25). | Pro 22:25 | U1 §38 point 6 | Ch 5 |
| MS-25 | **Wasted, with the eye and body,** under vexation: "My eye is wasted from grief; my soul and my body also" (Psa 31:9). | Psa 31:9 | U1 §38 | Ch 5 |
| MS-26 | **Bitter, under provocation.** Hannah, provoked year after year, "was deeply distressed" (1Sa 1:10; *nep̄eš* in the text: bitter of soul). | 1Sa 1:10 | part M | Ch 5 (already) |

| MS-27 | **Torn by its own anger.** "You who tear yourself in your anger" (Job 18:4; *nep̄eš*). Elihu's anger was at Job "because he justified himself rather than God" (Job 32:2; *nep̄eš*). | Job 18:4; 32:2 | U1 §38 | Ch 5 |
| MS-28 | **The life put at risk.** "whoever provokes him to anger forfeits his life" (Pro 20:2). Held with life and death (OT-08). | Pro 20:2 | U1 §38 | held (Ch 2) |

| MS-29 | **The body where the indignation lands:** "There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation" (Psa 38:3). Vexation removed from the heart and pain from the body together (Ecc 11:10). | Psa 38:3; Ecc 11:10 | U2 §66; U1 §38 | Ch 7 (already: Psa 38:3) |

| MS-30 | **Conscience beside the wrath:** "Therefore one must be in subjection, not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience" (Rom 13:5). | Rom 13:5 | U2 §66 (new as a reading) | Ch 8 |
| MS-31 | **The bosom where anger lodges** (Ecc 7:9). | Ecc 7:9 | U1 §38 | Ch 8 (already) |

- **Where the angry person's own heart or spirit is named** (U1 §38 point 1, counted): in the narratives it is rare (2Ki 6:11; Est 5:9; Act 7:54; Act 17:16; Eze 3:14). In the wisdom books it is frequent (Job 36:13; Pro 6:14; 14:29; 16:32; 19:3; Ecc 2:23; 7:3; 7:9; 11:10). The narratives show anger by what is done. **Kept as a count, without U1's "so that" clause** (rule 69).
- **In the narratives, the seat is often named by someone else** (U1 §38 point 3): Eliab names David's heart (1Sa 17:28); Jesus' anger is at his opponents' hardened heart (Mar 3:5).
